clause_text: The rent in respect of the Demised Premises shall commence from 1st April 2026 and shall be valid till 28th February 2027. Thereafter, the same may be extended further on mutual consent of both the parties.
risk_reason: Standard fixed-term clause with mutual renewal; no unilateral disadvantage to either party.
simplified_text: Your rental term runs from 1 April 2026 to 28 Feb 2027. It can only be extended if both you and the owner agree.
tip: Confirm the exact start and end dates match what was verbally agreed before signing.

clause_text: The Tenant shall pay to the Owner a monthly rent of Rs.25,000, excluding electricity and water bill. The rent shall be paid on or before 7th day of each month without fail.
risk_reason: Clear, standard rent clause with defined due date; no hidden charges.
simplified_text: You must pay Rs.25,000 rent by the 7th of every month, not including electricity or water.
tip: Set a monthly reminder a few days before the 7th to avoid late payment disputes.

clause_text: The Tenant shall pay to the Owner a monthly maintenance charge of Rs.2,000 towards the maintenance of Generator & Elevator, Salaries towards guards, Charges for Electricity Maintenance for Common Areas, Charges towards cleaning of Common Areas and towards maintaining the lawn.
risk_reason: Charge is itemized but fixed amount isn't tied to any receipts or cap on future increases.
simplified_text: You pay Rs.2,000/month extra for shared building costs like the generator, elevator, guards, and lawn upkeep.
tip: Ask if this maintenance amount can increase later and if so, under what conditions.

clause_text: The Tenant will pay to the Owner an interest-free refundable security deposit of Rs.75,000 vide cheque no 123456 dated 1st April 2026 at the time of signing the Rent Agreement.
risk_reason: Standard refundable deposit; interest-free is common practice and not unusually unfavorable.
simplified_text: You pay a refundable deposit of Rs.75,000 upfront, with no interest earned on it.
tip: Keep a copy of the cheque and this clause as proof of the deposit amount paid.

clause_text: The said amount of the Security deposit shall be refunded by the Owner to the Tenant at the time of handing over possession of the demised premises by the Tenant upon expiry or sooner termination of this Rent after adjusting any dues (if any) or cost towards damages caused by the negligence of the Tenant.
risk_reason: 'Any dues' and 'damages' are not defined or capped, giving the Owner discretion over deductions.
simplified_text: Your deposit will be returned when you move out, but the owner can subtract unpaid dues or damage costs first.
tip: Ask for a written, itemized list of any deductions before accepting the refunded amount.

clause_text: In case the Owner fails to refund the security deposit to the Tenant on early termination or expiry of the Rent agreement, the Tenant is entitled to hold possession of the Rented premises, without payment of rent and/or any other charges whatsoever, till such time the Owner refunds the security deposit to the Tenant.
risk_reason: Strongly protects the Tenant by giving leverage if the Owner delays the deposit refund.
simplified_text: If the owner doesn't return your deposit on time, you're allowed to stay in the property rent-free until they do.
tip: This clause favors you — keep proof of when you vacated in case you need to use it.

clause_text: The Tenant shall not sublet, assign or part with the demised premises in whole or part thereof to any person in any circumstances whatsoever and the same shall be used for the bonafide residential purposes only.
risk_reason: Absolute prohibition on subletting with no exceptions, even for short-term or family arrangements.
simplified_text: You cannot sublet or hand over the property to anyone else, under any circumstances, and must only use it to live in.
tip: Clarify with the owner whether temporary guests or family staying over counts as 'subletting'.

clause_text: That the day-to-day minor repairs will be the responsibility for the Tenant at his/her own expense. However, any structural or major repairs, if so required, shall be carried out by the Owner.
risk_reason: Fair and standard split of repair responsibility between minor (tenant) and major (owner) issues.
simplified_text: You pay for small repairs yourself; the owner is responsible for major structural repairs.
tip: Get a shared understanding in writing of what counts as 'minor' vs 'major' repair before disputes arise.

clause_text: No structural additions or alterations shall be made by the Tenant in the premises without the prior written consent of the Owner but the Tenant can install air-conditioners in the space provided and other electrical gadgets and make such changes for the purposes as may be necessary, at his own cost.
risk_reason: Reasonable restriction with a clear, tenant-friendly exception for common appliances like ACs.
simplified_text: You need the owner's written permission for structural changes, but you can install ACs and similar gadgets freely.
tip: Get any verbal permission for changes confirmed over text or email as a record.

clause_text: That the Owner shall hold the right to visit in person or through his authorized agent(s), servants, workmen etc., to enter upon the demised premises for inspection (not exceeding once in a month) or to carry out repairs / construction, as and when required.
risk_reason: Frequency is capped at once a month, but 'as and when required' for repairs is vague and could be used to justify more frequent entry.
simplified_text: The owner (or their staff) can visit your home for inspection up to once a month, and more often if repairs are needed.
tip: Ask for advance notice (e.g. 24-48 hours) to be added before any visit, even for repairs.

clause_text: That this Rent Agreement can be terminated before the expiry of this tenancy period by serving One month prior notice in writing by either party.
risk_reason: Mutual and balanced — both Owner and Tenant have equal notice rights and equal notice period.
simplified_text: Either you or the owner can end this agreement early by giving one month's written notice.
tip: Always send termination notice in writing (email or letter) to have a dated record.

clause_text: That in case, where the Premises are not vacated by the Tenant, at the termination of the Rent period, the Tenant will pay damages calculated at two times the rent for any period of occupation commencing from the expiry of the Rent period.
risk_reason: Punitive 2x rent penalty with no grace period for delays like finding new housing or logistics.
simplified_text: If you don't move out on time, you must pay double the normal rent for each extra day or month you stay.
tip: Negotiate a short grace period (e.g. 3-5 days) before the penalty rate applies, in case of moving delays.

clause_text: In case of any dispute to this agreement and the clauses herein, the same will be settled in the jurisdiction of the city civil courts.
risk_reason: Fixes jurisdiction to a single city's courts, which may be inconvenient or costly for a Tenant who later moves away.
simplified_text: Any legal dispute about this agreement must be handled in the courts of this specific city, not wherever you live later.
tip: If you're renting far from your hometown, weigh the cost of pursuing disputes in that specific city's courts.

clause_text: The rent shall be increased by 5% (Five Percent) once in every one year.
risk_reason: Fixed, transparent, and modest annual increase; standard practice, not exploitative.
simplified_text: Your rent goes up by 5% every year, so you know in advance how much more you'll pay.
tip: Calculate what your rent will be in years 2 and 3 so there are no surprises later.

clause_text: If fails to pay for a period of 2 months the owner can occupy the house premises.
risk_reason: Allows the owner to retake the property directly after just 2 months of missed rent, with no mention of legal notice or court process.
simplified_text: If you miss rent for 2 months, the owner can take back the house themselves, without going through a legal eviction process.
tip: This bypasses standard legal eviction procedure — ask for a formal notice period and legal process to be added instead.

clause_text: The LESSEES will pay to the LESSOR 10% increment in rent on completion of 12 months stay from the date of this agreement.
risk_reason: A 10% renewal increase is double the common 5% norm seen in comparable agreements, presenting a medium financial risk.
simplified_text: Your rent increases by 10% once you complete a full year of staying.
tip: Confirm whether this 10% applies to the base rent or the total including maintenance charges.

clause_text: The LESSOR holds the right to terminate the agreement if the LESSEE fails to pay the rent regularly for consecutive period of 2 months or commits a breach of any terms herein and can take possession of the premise.
risk_reason: Allows the owner to take possession directly after 2 months of missed rent without explicit legal notice or court process.
simplified_text: If you're late on rent for 2 months, or break almost any rule in this agreement, the owner can end the tenancy and take the house back themselves.
tip: Ask what specifically counts as a 'breach' and whether a formal notice period applies before repossession.

clause_text: If the lessee commits breach of any of the conditions here above mentioned notwithstanding the period herein above mentioned, the lessor shall be at liberty to revoke and or cancel the lease granted forthwith.
risk_reason: Allows immediate, unilateral cancellation for any breach with no cure period or advance notice given to the tenant.
simplified_text: Breaking almost any rule in this agreement lets the owner cancel your lease immediately, with no chance to fix the issue first.
tip: Negotiate a written cure period (e.g. 15 days to fix an issue) before the lease can be cancelled outright.

clause_text: The lessor or their authorized agents shall be entitled to enter upon the said house to inspect the conditions of the premises or to get repairs done or for other lawful purpose thereof at all reasonable times and the lessee shall allow them to so enter.
risk_reason: No fixed notice period or visit-frequency cap is defined; 'reasonable times' is subjective and owner-favorable.
simplified_text: The owner or their staff can enter your home for inspections or repairs whenever they consider it a reasonable time.
tip: Ask for a minimum notice period (e.g. 24 hours) to be added in writing before any entry.

clause_text: In case Customer decides to terminate the agreement before completion of 12 paid months, the customer will be liable to pay Procall for the balance months of services.
risk_reason: Requires paying for the entire remaining contract term even after ending the service early, with no reduction for unused time.
simplified_text: If you cancel early, you still have to pay for every remaining month left in the 12-month term.
tip: Try to negotiate a partial early-termination fee instead of full remaining balance liability.

clause_text: In case of dispute arising out of, or in relation to this Agreement between the parties hereto the same shall first be sought to be settled by arbitration governed by the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 and the rules framed hereunder.
risk_reason: Mandatory arbitration is legally standard in India but limits the option to go straight to court, which can be slower/costlier for an individual.
simplified_text: Any disagreement must first go through arbitration (a private legal process) rather than filing directly in court.
tip: Ask who bears the arbitration costs and where the arbitration will be held, since this can add expense.

clause_text: CHANGE OF TERMS: The terms and conditions of this agreement are subject to future change by the LANDLORD after the expiry of the agreed lease period upon a 30 day written notice setting forth such change delivered to the TENANT.
risk_reason: Only the landlord has unilateral power to change terms; tenant has no equivalent right or negotiation step mentioned.
simplified_text: After your lease term ends, the landlord can change the rules with just 30 days written notice, and you don't have an equal say.
tip: Ask whether you can decline the new terms and exit the lease if you disagree with the changes.

clause_text: TERMINATION: ...written notice, intention to terminate 2 month's rent to the LANDLORD in lieu of the notice should be paid by the TENANT, if he/she vacates, without giving notice.
risk_reason: A defined, capped penalty (2 months' rent) for skipping notice; reasonable in scope but still a meaningful cost.
simplified_text: If you move out without giving proper notice, you'll owe the landlord 2 months' rent instead.
tip: Set a calendar reminder well ahead of your planned move-out date to avoid this penalty entirely.

clause_text: VACATION OF SCHEDULE PREMISES: ...If the TENANT fail to vacate all possessions on or before the termination date the TENANT shall be liable for additional rent and damages due to LANDLORD'S loss of prospective new renters.
risk_reason: 'Loss of prospective new renters' is an open-ended, unquantified damages claim with no cap, favoring the landlord heavily.
simplified_text: If you don't fully move out on time, you could owe extra rent plus undefined damages for any renters the landlord claims to have lost because of the delay.
tip: Push to cap this penalty at a fixed daily/weekly rate instead of leaving it open-ended.

clause_text: PERIODIC REVISION OF RENT: The TENANT undertake to pay the LANDLORD the enhanced rent after every 11 (Eleven) months at the rate of 10% over the then existing rate of rent, in the event of the Rental Lease getting extended after the expiry of the earlier Rental Lease period.
risk_reason: Fixed percentage, applies only if the lease is renewed, and is transparent about timing and rate.
simplified_text: If you renew your lease, rent goes up by a fixed 10% each time, so future costs are predictable.
tip: Factor this 10% increase into your budget planning if you expect to stay beyond the first term.

clause_text: If the Lessee fails to pay the monthly rent in time, the Lessor shall have the liberty to resume the schedule premises without re-course to any action, legal or other wise.
risk_reason: Explicitly allows the owner to retake the property without any legal process for a single late payment, which is a serious departure from due process.
simplified_text: If you're even briefly late on rent, the owner can take back the property immediately, without going to court.
tip: This clause removes your legal protections entirely — strongly consider negotiating a grace period and formal notice requirement.

clause_text: The Owner shall have the right to terminate the tenancy if the tenant fails to pay the rents regularly for a consecutive period of 3 months or commits breach of any of the terms herein and take position of the premises.
risk_reason: Standard default clause with a reasonable three-month grace period before termination; 'take possession' language matches common boilerplate seen across comparable agreements.
simplified_text: If you miss 3 months of rent or break a rule in the agreement, the owner can end your tenancy and take back the property.
tip: Ask for clarity on what counts as a 'breach' beyond non-payment, since the wording is broad.

clause_text: Notwithstanding what is stated above, the agreement shall be revoked by the Lessor, if the Lessee is in default in the payment of the rent and/or other charges three months after the same have fallen due or if the Lessee commits breach of any terms and conditions of this agreement.
risk_reason: 3-month grace period before revocation is reasonable, but 'any breach' remains vague and broad.
simplified_text: You get 3 months of missed payments before the lease can be revoked, but almost any rule violation could also trigger it.
tip: Ask for a specific list of what counts as a serious breach, rather than an open-ended catch-all.

clause_text: You are being offered the position of [DESIGNATION] in the [DEPARTMENT] department, reporting to [REPORTING MANAGER].
risk_reason: Purely descriptive role clause with no obligations or risk; standard boilerplate.
simplified_text: This states your job title, department, and who you report to.
tip: Confirm this designation matches what was discussed verbally during the interview.

clause_text: Your employment will commence on [DATE OF JOINING]. You are required to report at [LOCATION] on the said date.
risk_reason: Standard joining clause; no ambiguity or one-sided terms.
simplified_text: You must start work and report to this location on the specified joining date.
tip: Make sure the reporting location matches what you expect (not a different city/branch).

clause_text: Your annual Cost to Company (CTC) shall be Rs. [AMOUNT]/- (Rupees [AMOUNT IN WORDS] only). The detailed breakup is provided in Annexure A.
risk_reason: CTC figure alone can be misleading if the Annexure A breakup isn't reviewed; large gaps between CTC and take-home pay are common.
simplified_text: Your total yearly package (CTC) is this amount, but the actual breakdown of what you take home is in a separate annexure.
tip: Always review Annexure A in detail — CTC often includes PF, gratuity, and variable pay that reduce your monthly take-home.

clause_text: You will be on probation for a period of [MONTHS] months from the date of joining. Confirmation shall be subject to satisfactory performance.
risk_reason: 'Satisfactory performance' is not defined by any measurable criteria, giving the employer broad discretion over confirmation.
simplified_text: You'll be on probation for a set number of months, and becoming a permanent employee depends on you performing well — though this isn't clearly defined.
tip: Ask HR what specific criteria or reviews determine 'satisfactory performance' before you sign.

clause_text: Standard working hours are [START TIME] to [END TIME], [DAYS] days a week. You are entitled to leaves as per the company's leave policy.
risk_reason: Standard working hours clause; leave policy is referenced but not detailed in this document.
simplified_text: These are your official work hours and days per week; leave entitlement follows a separate company policy.
tip: Request a copy of the actual leave policy document referenced here before joining.

clause_text: During probation: [DAYS] days notice. After confirmation: [DAYS] days notice by either party for termination of employment.
risk_reason: Notice period is mutual and applies equally to both employer and employee, which is fair and balanced.
simplified_text: You and the company must both give the same amount of notice to end your employment, and the period is shorter during probation.
tip: Note that the probation notice period is usually much shorter — useful if you need to exit early.

clause_text: You shall maintain confidentiality of all proprietary information during and after employment. Violation shall be grounds for immediate termination and legal action.
risk_reason: 'Proprietary information' is undefined and the confidentiality obligation extends indefinitely after employment, with legal action as a stated consequence for any violation.
simplified_text: You must keep company information secret forever, even after you leave — and breaking this could get you fired and sued, though what counts as confidential isn't clearly defined.
tip: Ask for a clear definition of what counts as 'proprietary information' and whether the obligation has any time limit after you leave.

clause_text: This offer is conditional upon: (a) satisfactory background verification; (b) submission of required documents; (c) medical fitness if required.
risk_reason: Offer can be revoked based on subjective 'satisfactory' verification with no clear standard or appeal process mentioned.
simplified_text: This job offer isn't final until you pass a background check, submit documents, and (if needed) a medical exam.
tip: Ask what happens if verification is delayed or a document is hard to obtain — does the offer expire?

clause_text: The lessor agrees to let-out the schedule premises for a monthly rent of 7000/- per month, and the lessee shall agree to pay the same on every month, by on or before 5th of Every English calendar month.
risk_reason: Standard monthly rent with a clear due date; no hidden terms.
simplified_text: You pay Rs.7,000 rent by the 5th of each month.
tip: Set a reminder a few days before the 5th each month.

clause_text: The lease will be for period of 11 (Eleven) months from the date of this Agreement, but it can be extended by mutual consent. The rent shall be enhanced Once in every 11 months @ 5% over the existing rent.
risk_reason: Standard 11-month term with a typical 5% renewal increase; common and not unusually unfavorable.
simplified_text: Your lease runs 11 months and can be renewed if both sides agree, with rent going up 5% each renewal.
tip: Confirm in writing before renewal whether the 5% increase applies.

clause_text: The lessee should not sub-let or underlet the schedule premises to any Other persons without written consent from the lessor.
risk_reason: Standard no-subletting clause requiring landlord consent; typical and reasonable.
simplified_text: You can't sublet the place to anyone else unless the owner agrees in writing.
tip: Get any subletting permission from the owner in writing, not verbally.

clause_text: Whereas the lessee shall agree to pay one month rent towards painting charges at the time of vacating the schedule premises.
risk_reason: A flat one-month-rent painting charge on exit is an added cost beyond the deposit, regardless of the property's actual condition.
simplified_text: When you move out, you must pay one full month's rent extra for repainting, no matter the condition of the walls.
tip: Ask if this charge is waived if the walls are already in good condition, and get any waiver in writing.

clause_text: The Tenant shall pay a monthly rent of Rs.8000 on or before 5th of every month. Rent will be start from at the time of occupation. The rent enhancement shall be increased at 10% after 11 months.
risk_reason: A 10% renewal increase is double the common 5% norm seen in comparable agreements, which is a meaningfully steeper cost escalation.
simplified_text: You pay Rs.8,000 rent monthly, but after 11 months your rent jumps up by 10% if you continue — higher than the usual 5% seen elsewhere.
tip: Try to negotiate this down to the more typical 5% before signing, or clarify it upfront if it's non-negotiable.

clause_text: The Tenant has to pay the security deposit amount of Rs. 60000... shall not carry any interest but will be refundable to the Tenant on the termination of Tenancy. After deducting any dues in rent/electricity/damages etc.
risk_reason: Standard interest-free refundable deposit with deductions limited to actual dues; common practice.
simplified_text: You pay Rs.60,000 deposit, refunded when you leave, minus any unpaid rent, electricity, or damage costs.
tip: Do a joint walkthrough with the owner before vacating to agree on any deductions upfront.

clause_text: The Tenant shall pay one month rent towards painting and cleaning charges at the time of vacating the schedule premises.
risk_reason: A flat one-month-rent charge for painting and cleaning applies regardless of the property's actual condition on exit.
simplified_text: When you move out, you owe one full month's rent extra for painting and cleaning, no matter how clean the place is.
tip: Ask if this can be waived or reduced if you leave the place in good condition, and get any agreement in writing.

clause_text: Confidential Information shall not include information which Recipient can demonstrate is or becomes available to the public through no breach of this Agreement.
risk_reason: Standard exception to confidentiality for public domain information, protecting the recipient from overreach.
simplified_text: Information that is already public is not considered confidential.
tip: Ensure you keep records showing that the information was already public before you signed.

clause_text: All obligations with respect to non-trade secret Confidential Information shall survive termination or expiration of this Agreement for a period of five (5) years from the date of termination.
risk_reason: The 5-year survival period is longer than typical 1-2 year periods, posing a medium risk of accidental breach long after the contract ends.
simplified_text: You must keep non-trade secret information confidential for 5 years after this agreement ends.
tip: Set a calendar reminder for 5 years post-termination to formally close out compliance tracking.

clause_text: The Receiving Party shall not retain any copies, extracts or reproductions in any form, and must permanently destroy the same and certify such destruction in writing.
risk_reason: A mandatory destruction certificate creates an administrative burden and liability if a single digital artifact is missed in backups.
simplified_text: You must destroy all copies of the confidential information and provide a written certificate proving you did so.
tip: Have your IT department run a full sweep of servers and backups to ensure no stray files remain before certifying.

clause_text: Subject to applicable arbitration provisions, the courts at Kolkata, West Bengal shall have exclusive jurisdiction over all disputes arising out of or relating to this Agreement.
risk_reason: Fixes jurisdiction to a single city's courts (Kolkata), which may be inconvenient or costly if the receiving party is based elsewhere.
simplified_text: Any legal arguments about this contract must be handled in the courts of Kolkata.
tip: If you are not based in Kolkata, try to negotiate for jurisdiction in your own city or a neutral location.

clause_text: The Receiving Party understands and agrees that the Disclosing Party makes no representation, warranty or guaranty, expressed or implied, as to the accuracy or completeness of the Confidential Information.
risk_reason: Disclaiming accuracy of provided information shifts the risk of relying on flawed or incomplete data entirely onto the receiving party.
simplified_text: The party sharing the information does not guarantee that it is completely accurate or complete.
tip: Independently verify any financial or technical data before making business decisions based on it.

clause_text: That you are a regular defaulter in paying rent to my client and now the rent for 10 months has become due from you. I call upon you to pay the whole of the arrears of rent within 2 months.
risk_reason: A formal legal demand for accumulated rent arrears poses a severe immediate financial and legal threat.
simplified_text: You have missed 10 months of rent and must pay the full amount owed within 2 months.
tip: If you dispute the arrears amount, reply immediately through a lawyer rather than ignoring the notice.

clause_text: I require you to quit, vacate and deliver the peaceful and vacant possession of the said premises to my client within 30 days from the receipt of this notice failing which my client will start eviction proceedings.
risk_reason: This is a formal termination of tenancy backed by an explicit threat of court proceedings and eviction.
simplified_text: You must move out within 30 days, or the landlord will take you to court.
tip: Consult a tenant rights lawyer immediately to review if the 30-day notice complies with your original lease agreement.

clause_text: If the tenant causes damage to the property by any means, the landlord has the right to ask the tenant to vacate the property immediately without serving the standard notice period.
risk_reason: Allows for immediate eviction based on 'damage by any means', which is highly subjective and bypasses standard notice periods.
simplified_text: The landlord can kick you out immediately without notice if they believe you have damaged the property.
tip: Take a detailed video walkthrough of the property's condition on the day you move in to protect against false damage claims.

clause_text: In the event of a breach of any term of this NDA, the Disclosing Party shall be entitled to seek immediate injunctive relief without the necessity of proving actual damages.
risk_reason: Allows the disclosing party to get a court order stopping your business activities immediately without even having to prove you caused them financial harm.
simplified_text: If you break this agreement, the other party can immediately get a court order against you without proving actual financial loss.
tip: Request that 'injunctive relief' requires a demonstration of reasonable evidence of harm before being granted.

clause_text: You are hereby called upon to pay a sum of Rs. 15,000/- towards the cost of this legal notice within 15 days of receipt.
risk_reason: It is standard for lawyers to demand the cost of the notice from the recipient, but a Rs. 15,000 fee is steep and represents a direct financial demand.
simplified_text: The landlord's lawyer is demanding you pay Rs. 15,000 to cover the cost of them sending this notice to you.
tip: You are not legally obligated to pay the opposing lawyer's notice fee unless a court explicitly orders costs against you.

clause_text: Both the parties have agreed to set a lock-in period of 12 months during which neither the Licensor shall ask the licensee to vacate the premises, nor the licensee shall vacate the premises on his own during the lock-in period. In spite of this mandatory clause, if the licensee leaves the premises... he shall pay to the licensor license fee for the remaining lock-in period at the rate of agreed upon in the agreement.
risk_reason: Forcing the tenant to pay the full remaining rent for the entire lock-in period if they leave early is a severe financial penalty, typical in commercial leases but highly punitive for residential.
simplified_text: You cannot leave for the first 12 months. If you do leave early, you still have to pay rent for the rest of those 12 months.
tip: Negotiate a standard 1-2 month notice penalty for breaking the lock-in, rather than paying for all remaining months.

clause_text: In the event of the Licensees failing and / or neglecting to remove themselves and / or his articles from the said premises on expiry or sooner determination of this Agreement, the Licensors shall be entitled to recover damages at the rate of double the daily amount of compensation per day.
risk_reason: A double-rent penalty for overstaying without any specified grace period is highly punitive and grants the landlord leverage to extract exorbitant fees.
simplified_text: If you don't move out exactly on the last day of the agreement, you will be charged double the normal rent for every extra day you stay.
tip: Ask for a 7-day grace period in case of unavoidable moving delays before the double penalty kicks in.

clause_text: That the Licensees shall pay to the Licensors the following amount per month: a) Rs. 12000/- per month for the first 12 months, b) Rs. 13000/- per month for the next 12 months, c) Rs. 14000/- per month for the next 12 months.
risk_reason: The rent escalations are clearly defined, staggered transparently, and agreed upon upfront. Classified as payment per our standardization rule.
simplified_text: Your rent is Rs. 12,000 for the first year, Rs. 13,000 for the second year, and Rs. 14,000 for the third year.
tip: Ensure your budget can handle the predetermined increases in the second and third years.

clause_text: That the Licensee shall not claim any tenancy right and shall not have any right to transfer, assign, and sublet or grant any license or sub-license in respect of the Licensed Premises.
risk_reason: Absolute prohibition on subletting with no exceptions. Standard for Leave and License agreements but strictly restricts tenant flexibility.
simplified_text: You cannot claim permanent tenancy rights, and you cannot sublet or hand over the property to anyone else.
tip: Clarify if having family or guests stay for an extended period could be misinterpreted as subletting.

clause_text: The members of the society has intimated my client that they are filing a complaint under 107/145 of Criminal Procedure Code before Executive Magistrate against the said tenant for causing nuisance and disturbance to the society. Further, it is hereby informed to you that it will be your responsibility, and you will also be criminally liable for the deeds of the tenant.
risk_reason: A legal notice explicitly threatening criminal liability (CrPC 107/145) for nuisance is a severe legal escalation beyond a standard civil dispute.
simplified_text: The building society is threatening to file a criminal complaint against you for causing a disturbance, and the landlord is holding you criminally responsible.
tip: Do not ignore criminal threat notices; consult a lawyer immediately to respond and defuse the situation.

clause_text: That you addressee are not paying rent to my client consecutively w.e.f from [DATE] in lieu of adjustment of security deposit against the two month rent of the premise.
risk_reason: The landlord is formally disputing the tenant's attempt to use the security deposit as the final months' rent, which is a common but often legally contentious practice.
simplified_text: The landlord is rejecting your attempt to skip paying the last two months of rent by using your security deposit to cover it.
tip: Most agreements prohibit using the deposit as rent; you usually must pay the final months and wait for a separate deposit refund.

clause_text: The Property Manager or the Landlord shall have the right to enter the Demised Premises at any time during the day or night without any prior notice to the Tenant in case of suspected emergencies or routine checks.
risk_reason: Allowing entry 'day or night without prior notice' for 'routine checks' strips the tenant of basic privacy rights and quiet enjoyment.
simplified_text: The landlord or manager can enter your home at any time, day or night, without warning you.
tip: Insist on a mandatory 24-hour written notice for any entry that is not a life-threatening emergency.

clause_text: The Lessor or his authorized agents shall be permitted to enter the Schedule Property for inspection only on weekends between 10:00 AM and 5:00 PM, subject to providing a minimum of 48 hours prior written notice via email or WhatsApp.
risk_reason: Provides a generous 48-hour notice period and restricts visits to reasonable weekend hours, highly protective of tenant privacy.
simplified_text: The owner can only visit on weekends during the day, and they must message you at least 48 hours in advance.
tip: Ensure the owner sticks to the agreed WhatsApp or email notice method so you have a written record of visits.

clause_text: The Landlord may enter the premises to show the property to prospective buyers or new tenants during the last 60 days of the lease term, provided reasonable notice is given.
risk_reason: While showing the property is standard, 'reasonable notice' is undefined and open to interpretation, potentially causing daily disruptions at the end of the lease.
simplified_text: In the last two months, the landlord can bring potential new tenants to view the house if they give you 'reasonable' notice.
tip: Define 'reasonable notice' as a specific timeframe (e.g., 24 hours) in writing before signing.

clause_text: The Tenant assumes all responsibility for the maintenance of the HVAC system, plumbing, and electrical wiring within the premises, and must replace any units that fail during the term of this Lease at their own cost.
risk_reason: Forces the tenant to bear the capital cost of replacing major structural/appliance systems (HVAC, plumbing) which should be the landlord's asset responsibility.
simplified_text: You are responsible for fixing and even replacing the AC, plumbing, and electrical systems if they break.
tip: Refuse this clause. Tenants should only be responsible for routine minor maintenance, not capital replacements.

clause_text: The Lessee shall bear the cost of routine servicing of air conditioners and daily sweeping of the premises, while the Lessor agrees to cover any costs related to structural wear and tear, seepage, or major electrical faults.
risk_reason: Standard, fair distribution of maintenance: tenant handles daily upkeep, landlord handles structural and major repairs.
simplified_text: You pay for AC servicing and regular cleaning; the owner pays for major structural repairs and water leaks.
tip: Report any water leaks immediately in writing so the landlord cannot claim you caused secondary damage by delaying.

clause_text: Any dispute arising out of this Agreement shall be referred to a sole arbitrator appointed exclusively by the First Party. The decision of the arbitrator shall be final and binding.
risk_reason: Giving one party the exclusive right to choose the sole arbitrator inherently biases the dispute resolution process against the other party.
simplified_text: If there is a legal fight, the landlord gets to pick the person (arbitrator) who decides who wins.
tip: Demand that the arbitrator be chosen by 'mutual consent' of both parties.

clause_text: The courts of New Delhi alone shall have exclusive jurisdiction to try and entertain any disputes arising out of this Agreement.
risk_reason: Standard jurisdiction clause assuming both parties are operating out of New Delhi. Low risk if local.
simplified_text: Any court cases about this contract must happen in New Delhi.
tip: Only agree to this if you actually live or work in New Delhi; otherwise, negotiate for your home city.

clause_text: The Company reserves the right to modify the terms, scope of work, and compensation structure of this Consultancy Agreement at its sole discretion by providing a 7-day email notice.
risk_reason: Allows one party to unilaterally change the rules and pay structure of the contract with minimal notice, rendering the original agreement unstable.
simplified_text: The company can change your pay or your job duties whenever they want, with only 7 days' warning.
tip: Amendments should always require the written consent of both parties, not just a notification.

clause_text: No modification, variation, or amendment to this Agreement shall be valid or binding unless made in writing and duly signed by both the Landlord and the Tenant.
risk_reason: Standard protective clause ensuring neither party can secretly or unilaterally change the rules without the other's signature.
simplified_text: This agreement can only be changed if both you and the landlord agree in writing and sign it.
tip: If the landlord promises something verbally, insist they add it to the written agreement and sign it.

clause_text: The Consultant shall not directly or indirectly provide services to any competitor of the Company within India for a period of two (2) years following the termination of this Agreement.
risk_reason: A 2-year nationwide non-compete is highly restrictive, potentially preventing the consultant from earning a livelihood in their field post-termination.
simplified_text: You are not allowed to work for any competing company in India for 2 years after leaving this job.
tip: Non-competes in India are generally void under Section 27 of the Contract Act, but fighting them in court is expensive. Try to strike this out.

clause_text: The Tenant shall not keep any pets on the demised premises without the prior written consent of the Landlord, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld.
risk_reason: Standard pet restriction but with a built-in fairness clause ('shall not be unreasonably withheld') giving the tenant leverage.
simplified_text: You need the landlord's permission to keep a pet, but they cannot say no without a good reason.
tip: Get the written permission for your specific pet via email before moving in.

clause_text: In the event of delayed payment of the monthly rent beyond the 10th of the month, the Lessee shall be liable to pay a late fee of Rs. 500 per day for every day of delay.
risk_reason: A daily late fee of Rs. 500 accumulates rapidly (Rs. 15,000/month) and is disproportionately punitive compared to standard interest rates on late payments.
simplified_text: If you pay rent after the 10th, you will be fined Rs. 500 for every single day you are late.
tip: Negotiate a flat, one-time late fee (e.g., Rs. 1000) rather than a compounding daily penalty.

clause_text: The Lessee shall pay a sum of Rs. 50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) as an advance token amount, which shall be non-refundable if the Lessee decides not to execute the final lease deed.
risk_reason: Making a token advance entirely non-refundable places the financial risk solely on the tenant if negotiations fall through due to the landlord's unreasonableness.
simplified_text: You pay Rs. 50,000 to hold the property, but you lose that money if you decide not to sign the final lease.
tip: Add a condition stating the token is refundable if the landlord changes the agreed terms before signing.

clause_text: The Landlord reserves the right to terminate this tenancy immediately and forcefully evict the tenant by locking the premises if the tenant is found engaging in any unlawful activities.
risk_reason: Allows for extra-judicial forced eviction ('locking the premises') without due process or a court order, violating Indian tenancy laws.
simplified_text: The landlord claims the right to lock you out of the house immediately if they think you are doing something illegal.
tip: Under Indian law, a landlord cannot forcefully lock you out without a court order, regardless of what the contract says.

clause_text: The Lessor or his authorized agents shall have the right to enter upon the schedule premises at any hour of the day or night, without prior notification to the Lessee, for the purpose of inspecting the state of repairs or carrying out necessary alterations or additions.
risk_reason: Grants the landlord unrestricted entry at any time of day or night without notice, completely violating the tenant's right to quiet enjoyment and privacy.
simplified_text: The landlord or their agents can enter the property at any time, day or night, without telling you first, to inspect or make changes.
tip: Insist on a clause requiring at least 24 hours prior written notice and restricting entry to reasonable daytime hours (e.g., 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM), except in emergencies.

clause_text: The Landlord reserves the absolute right to inspect the premises once in every calendar month during reasonable daytime hours (between 10:00 AM and 5:00 PM) with a prior written notice of 24 hours given to the Tenant.
risk_reason: Contains balanced terms with reasonable time restrictions and a mandatory notice period.
simplified_text: The landlord can inspect the property once a month during normal daytime hours, but must give you 24 hours' written notice first.
tip: This is a standard and fair clause. Ensure the landlord adheres to the 24-hour notice requirement.

clause_text: The Company shall have the absolute right to access, monitor, intercept, and search all electronic communications, files, and data stored on any device, network, or server provided by the Company to the Employee, at any time and without prior notice.
risk_reason: Allows broad corporate monitoring of company-provided assets, which is a standard industry practice but must be clearly separated from personal devices to protect employee privacy.
simplified_text: The company can monitor and search any file, email, or message on company-provided computers or phones at any time without warning.
tip: Avoid using company-provided devices, networks, or work accounts for any personal communications or storage.

clause_text: The Employer reserves the right to monitor and access the Employee's personal personal electronic devices, including but not limited to personal mobile phones and laptops, whenever connected to the corporate network, to audit for compliance with security policies.
risk_reason: Invades personal privacy by claiming a right to monitor personal devices simply because they connected to the company's network.
simplified_text: The company can monitor your personal phone or laptop if you connect it to the office Wi-Fi or network.
tip: Negotiate to delete reference to 'personal electronic devices'. Company access should be strictly limited to corporate-owned hardware.

clause_text: The Disclosing Party hereby grants the Receiving Party a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable right of access to its proprietary database solely for the purpose of executing the project services, subject to immediate revocation at the Disclosing Party's sole discretion.
risk_reason: Grants access but makes it highly unstable because the disclosing party can revoke it arbitrarily at any time, potentially stalling the service provider's work.
simplified_text: You are given temporary access to the client's database to do your work, but they can cut off your access at any time without warning.
tip: Add a clause stating that access cannot be unreasonably revoked if it prevents you from meeting your contractual deadlines, or that deadlines will be extended if access is cut off.

clause_text: The Consultant shall be provided secure, credentialed access to the Client's premises and internal servers during standard business hours, provided that the Consultant complies with all IT security policies and signs the visitor register upon entry.
risk_reason: Standard operational clause providing secure, clear access controls linked to security compliance.
simplified_text: You will get safe access to the client's office and servers during work hours, as long as you follow their security rules and sign in.
tip: Ensure you receive written copies of the client's IT security guidelines before starting your consulting services.

clause_text: The Tenant shall permit the Landlord or their authorized representatives to access the premises at any time for the purpose of displaying the property to prospective buyers or future tenants, without requirement of prior scheduling.
risk_reason: Forces the tenant to allow unscheduled, random showings to strangers at any time of day, disrupting privacy and security.
simplified_text: The landlord can bring prospective buyers or new tenants to look at your rented home at any time without booking an appointment.
tip: Restrict showings to the last 30 or 60 days of the tenancy, limit them to specific hours (e.g., weekends 11 AM - 4 PM), and require at least 24 hours' notice.

clause_text: During the last thirty (30) days of the lease term, the Tenant shall, upon receiving a 24-hour advance verbal request, permit the Landlord to show the premises to prospective tenants during reasonable daytime hours.
risk_reason: Standard, fair clause that restricts viewings to the end of the tenancy, demands reasonable hours, and requires notice.
simplified_text: In your final month, you must let the landlord show the property to new renters, provided they give you 24 hours' notice and visit during reasonable hours.
tip: Verify that 'reasonable daytime hours' is understood, preferably specifying hours like 10:00 AM to 6:00 PM.

clause_text: The Company retains the right to physical access to the Consultant's private office premises at any time to audit, inspect, or retrieve any physical documents or storage drives containing the Company's proprietary information.
risk_reason: Gives the client physical entry rights into the independent contractor's separate office, bypassing local privacy and trespass protections.
simplified_text: The client can enter your own private office to inspect or take documents and drives containing their business information.
tip: Remove this entirely. The client should request the return of information in writing, rather than having physical entry rights to your premises.

clause_text: All access tokens, cryptographic keys, and user credentials provided to the Partner to facilitate software integration shall remain the sole property of the Disclosing Party and must be deleted within forty-eight (48) hours of contract termination.
risk_reason: Clear security policy outlining access cleanup post-contract termination.
simplified_text: All digital access keys and passwords must be deleted within 48 hours after the contract ends.
tip: Ensure your IT team has a process in place to revoke and delete all client-provided keys promptly upon termination to avoid security non-compliance.

clause_text: The Licensee shall grant the Licensor absolute, unfettered access to all local servers hosting the licensed software at any hour, without notice, to verify compliance with license limits and search for unauthorized copies.
risk_reason: Grants the software vendor intrusive, unannounced access to the buyer's internal IT systems, posing severe cybersecurity and operational risks.
simplified_text: The software seller can log into or inspect your company's local computer servers at any time, without warning, to check license counts.
tip: Replace physical or unannounced server access with a standard clause allowing audit of license reports, or require pre-scheduled audits conducted in the presence of your IT staff.

clause_text: Any audit of the Licensee's systems to verify licensing compliance shall be conducted upon thirty (30) business days' prior written notice, during standard business hours, no more than once per calendar year, and in a manner that does not disrupt Licensee's operations.
risk_reason: Standard license audit clause protecting the licensee from operational disruption and intrusive unannounced checks.
simplified_text: Licensing compliance audits must be scheduled 30 business days in advance, can happen only once a year during work hours, and cannot disrupt your business.
tip: Ensure the clause also states that each party will bear its own costs for such audits, unless a material license deficit (e.g., >5%) is found.

clause_text: The Company reserves the right to modify, alter, amend, or rewrite this Agreement, its policies, benefits, compensation structures, or rules of employment at any time at its sole discretion, without prior notice or consent of the Employee.
risk_reason: Allows the employer to unilaterally change core employment terms, including salary and benefits, without notice or consent, which is highly exploitative.
simplified_text: The company can change this contract, your salary, benefits, or work rules at any time, without asking you or letting you know beforehand.
tip: Insist on a clause stating that any modification to the core terms of the agreement (especially compensation and role) must be in writing and signed by both parties.

clause_text: No amendment, modification, or variation of this Agreement shall be valid or binding unless it is made in writing, refers explicitly to this Agreement, and is executed by the duly authorized representatives of both Parties.
risk_reason: Standard bilateral amendment clause that protects both parties from verbal or unilateral contract changes.
simplified_text: No changes to this contract are valid unless they are written down, mention this contract, and are signed by both parties.
tip: Keep a signed, physical or digital copy of any subsequent amendments or addendums alongside your original contract.

clause_text: The Landlord shall have the right to amend the rules of occupancy, maintenance fees, or utility charges of the rented premises at any time by giving a seven (7) day notice to the Tenant, and such amendments shall automatically bind the Tenant.
risk_reason: Enables the landlord to unilaterally inflate maintenance fees or enforce restrictive living rules on extremely short notice.
simplified_text: The landlord can change the house rules, maintenance fees, or utility costs at any time by giving you a 7-day notice, and you must follow them.
tip: Negotiate to limit any changes in recurring charges to the annual lease renewal cycle, or require at least 30 days' notice with the tenant's right to terminate without penalty if they disagree.

clause_text: The Lessor and Lessee agree that any modifications or amendments to the rent amount, security deposit, or duration of this lease shall be executed strictly through a written addendum signed by both parties and duly registered under the Indian Registration Act, 1908.
risk_reason: Strongly protects the tenant by requiring written, signed, and registered addendums for major changes, in compliance with Indian legal requirements.
simplified_text: Any changes to your rent, security deposit, or lease length must be written, signed by both you and the landlord, and legally registered.
tip: In India, leases of 12 months or longer must be registered. Make sure any amendment to a registered lease is also registered to remain legally enforceable.

clause_text: The Client reserves the right to amend the scope of work, project delivery timelines, and payment milestone amounts unilaterally at any stage of the project by sending an electronic mail notification to the Consultant.
risk_reason: Grants the client unilateral control over work deliverables and compensation, allowing them to expand scope or slash pay without the consultant's consent.
simplified_text: The client can change the amount of work you do, your deadlines, and how much they pay you for milestones simply by sending you an email.
tip: Modify this to state that any change in scope of work or compensation must be mutually agreed upon in writing and signed via a Change Order or Addendum.

clause_text: Any adjustment or variation in the scope of services, project milestones, or fees must be proposed in writing and shall only become effective upon the mutual signature of a formal Change Order by both the Client and the Consultant.
risk_reason: Standard professional consulting framework requiring mutual consent and written Change Orders for project shifts.
simplified_text: Any changes to your work tasks, milestones, or fees must be agreed upon and signed by both you and the client using a formal Change Order document.
tip: Do not begin performing extra or modified work until the Change Order is fully signed by an authorized client representative.

clause_text: This Agreement contains the entire understanding between the parties, and the Company reserves the sole power to interpret and update the definitions of terms herein without recourse to the other party.
risk_reason: Gives the company absolute power to change the actual meaning of contract terms after signing, rendering the original agreement terms meaningless.
simplified_text: The company has the sole right to interpret and change what the terms in this contract mean, and you cannot dispute their interpretation.
tip: Delete the phrase allowing one party sole power to interpret definitions. Interpretation of disputes should rely on mutual agreement or independent arbitration.

clause_text: This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties and supersedes all prior discussions. No waiver or modification of any provision shall be valid unless in writing and signed by both Parties.
risk_reason: Standard 'integration' or 'entire agreement' clause preventing oral modifications or reliance on unwritten promises.
simplified_text: This written contract is the final and complete agreement. No verbal promises or emails can change it unless both parties sign a written modification.
tip: Ensure that any pre-signing verbal promises, emails, or assurances you rely on are explicitly written into this document before signing.

clause_text: The Disclosing Party may update the list of Protected Proprietary Materials or extend the definition of Confidential Information at any time by written notice, which shall immediately apply retroactively to all information shared since the initiation of discussions.
risk_reason: Applies new confidentiality classifications retroactively, creating compliance risks where the receiving party might have unknowingly handled older data without proper controls.
simplified_text: The other company can change the definition of confidential information and make it apply backward to things they already shared with you.
tip: Amend this so that retroactive updates are disallowed, or require at least 15 days to implement security measures for newly designated materials.

clause_text: No failure or delay by either party in exercising any right under this Agreement shall operate as a waiver thereof, nor shall any single or partial exercise of any right preclude any other or further exercise thereof.
risk_reason: Standard 'no waiver' protection ensuring that a temporary delay in enforcing rights does not permanently change or amend the contract rules.
simplified_text: If a party delays or forgets to enforce a rule once, it does not mean they have waived their right to enforce that rule in the future.
tip: This is standard legalese that protects legal rights; it is safe to accept without modification.

clause_text: The Employee agrees to comply with the Company's Employee Handbook and Code of Conduct, which may be revised, amended, or supplemented by the Company from time to time, and such modifications shall be binding upon publication.
risk_reason: Allows ongoing changes to office rules and conduct handbooks. Generally acceptable as long as it does not affect core terms like compensation, notice period, or role description.
simplified_text: You must follow the company's employee handbook, which the company can change or update whenever they want.
tip: Request that the company provide written notifications whenever major updates are made to the handbook, especially regarding leave policies or disciplinary measures.

clause_text: The Service Provider shall have the unilateral right to amend the pricing schedules, service level agreements, or technical specifications of the cloud hosting services with a 30-day electronic notice to the Customer.
risk_reason: Gives the provider power to raise prices or lower service levels unilaterally, but mitigates risk by requiring a 30-day notice, allowing the client time to react.
simplified_text: The hosting provider can change prices, service quality rules, or technical settings after giving you a 30-day notice.
tip: Negotiate for a price lock during the initial term of the contract, or add a right to terminate the contract without penalty if they increase prices by more than 10%.

clause_text: The Tenant shall pay a monthly rent of INR 25,000 (Rupees Twenty-Five Thousand Only) on or before the 5th day of each calendar month. Any delay in rent payment shall attract an interest fee of 18% per annum calculated daily.
risk_reason: While rent amounts are clear, an 18% per annum interest rate calculated daily is a high penalty rate for minor rent delays.
simplified_text: You must pay INR 25,000 rent by the 5th of every month. If you are late, you will be charged a penalty interest rate of 18% per year, calculated for each late day.
tip: Ask to lower the late penalty rate to a reasonable amount (e.g., 10% per annum) or negotiate a 5-day grace period before interest begins to accrue.

clause_text: The Tenant has deposited a sum of INR 1,50,000 (Rupees One Lakh Fifty Thousand Only) as an interest-free security deposit. The Landlord shall refund this deposit within 7 days of the Tenant vacating the premises, after deducting any unpaid rent, utility bills, or physical damages.
risk_reason: Clearly states the security deposit amount and commits the landlord to a swift refund timeline upon vacancy.
simplified_text: You paid a security deposit of INR 1,50,000. The landlord must return this within 7 days after you move out, minus any actual unpaid bills or property damage.
tip: Ensure you conduct a joint walk-through of the property with the landlord upon moving out and take photos to prevent unfair damage deductions.

clause_text: The Tenant shall not sub-let, assign, or transfer the possession of the rented premises or any part thereof to any other person under any circumstances, without the express prior written consent of the Landlord.
risk_reason: Standard and fair subletting restriction aimed at protecting the landlord's property from unauthorized occupancy.
simplified_text: You cannot rent out or transfer this property (or any part of it) to someone else unless you get the landlord's written permission first.
tip: If you plan to have a flatmate or co-occupant who is not on the lease, declare this to the landlord in writing before signing.

clause_text: The Landlord shall be entitled to forfeit the entire security deposit of INR 2,00,000 in the event that the Tenant terminates this lease for any reason prior to the completion of the 11-month lock-in period, regardless of notice provided.
risk_reason: Extremely punitive termination clause that results in total forfeiture of a large security deposit even if ample notice is provided.
simplified_text: If you leave the property before the 11-month lock-in period ends, the landlord will keep your entire INR 2,00,000 security deposit, no matter how much notice you give.
tip: Negotiate to remove or shorten the lock-in period, or request that the penalty be limited to one month's rent rather than the complete security deposit.

clause_text: Either party may terminate this agreement by giving two (2) months' prior written notice to the other party. Upon expiration of the notice period, the Tenant shall hand over peaceful possession of the premises.
risk_reason: Standard, balanced mutual termination clause with a reasonable notice period.
simplified_text: Either you or the landlord can end this agreement by giving 2 months' written notice.
tip: Confirm that there is no lock-in period that conflicts with this 2-month notice clause.

clause_text: The Company may terminate the Employee's service immediately and without notice or compensation in the event of gross misconduct, material breach of policy, fraud, or conviction of a criminal offense.
risk_reason: Standard 'termination for cause' clause with no notice or severance required for egregious behavior.
simplified_text: The company can fire you immediately without pay or notice if you commit fraud, break serious policies, or engage in gross misconduct.
tip: Verify that 'gross misconduct' or 'material breach' is clearly defined in the employee handbook to avoid arbitrary termination.

clause_text: The Client shall release payment for approved invoices within ninety (90) business days from the date of physical receipt of the invoice from the Consultant.
risk_reason: A 90-day payment term is highly unfavorable to consultants and freelancers, creating severe cashflow gaps.
simplified_text: The client has up to 90 days to pay your invoice after they receive it.
tip: Negotiate to reduce payment terms to a standard 30 days, or add a late payment interest clause of 1.5% per month.
